title: DP World Tour Championship: Eugenio Chacarra edges back ahead of Rory McIlroy in Race to Dubai battle ahead of final day
article_text:
Rory McIlroy and Eugenio Chacarra sit four strokes back heading into the final day of the DP World Tour Championship; McIlroy needs solo fourth or better to have any chance of overtaking Chacarra in the Race to Dubai standings; watch live on Sunday from 6.30am on Sky Sports Golf

Eugenio Chacarra is eyeing more than just holding off Rory McIlroy to Race to Dubai victory at the DP World Tour Championship, following a strong finish to his third round.

Chacarra entered the week with a 533.93-point lead over McIlroy in the season-long standings, having won three times this year, only to lose ground with rounds of 72 and 71 over the first two days at Jumeirah Golf Estates.

McIlroy temporarily moved above Chacarra into projected top spot, as he chases a record-equalling eighth Order of Merit title, with the world No 2 also briefly jumping to the top of the leaderboard before stuttering to a third-round 72.

Chacarra made nine birdies - including four in his last six holes - to post a four-under 68 and join McIlroy on five under, four strokes behind leader Tyrrell Hatton, but the Spaniard remains hopeful of challenging for tournament victory and 'Dubai double'.

"A lot of good and a lot of bad," Chacarra said about his performance. It has been a grind and I've been fighting. I've played all year on DP World Tour and I've played a lot.

"I want to really win that ranking, so I want to show the world I'm capable of playing under pressure. I think, so far, I've been doing that.

"I just want to win the tournament. I'm not far away. I know if I win the tournament, I win the ranking, so that's what I wanted to do in Abu Dhabi and I want to do it here.

"That's what we prepare for and I'm going to have a chance on Sunday. That's what we dream of since I was little is to win big events on Sunday.

"I'm ready. I love the game of golf. I love practising. I work so hard for these moments, and I'm going to go out there and enjoy it. Not a lot of people can enjoy this moment and have a chance to win the Race to Dubai."

Nine players started the week with a mathematical chance of topping the season-long standings, with South Africa's Jayden Schaper - needing a win and results to go his way - five strokes back and Jon Rahm a further shot behind.

McIlroy needs solo fourth or better to have any chance of surpassing Chacarra, who can guarantee the Order of Merit with victory, with the Spaniard still heading into the final round top of the projected Race to Dubai standings.

"There's a number of scenarios that could unfold tomorrow," former Ryder Cup captain Paul McGinley told Sky Sports. "I don't think Jon Rahm is not out of it yet - I could still see him coming through with a really strong last throw of the dice.

"I think Rory [McIlroy] will reset and [Eugenio] Chacarra is going to battle some way or another. I don't think he's going to win the tournament, but he's going to really make it difficult for those guys.

"I think there are a few little things that can bob and weave there. At the moment, it does look like Chacarra is the favourite for the Race to Dubai. Rory has fallen a lot off the pace and it's going to take a big reset now for him tomorrow to really go at it and shoot a low score.

"McIlroy's still there, or thereabouts and he will reset overnight, so I expect a better Rory coming out tomorrow. If he can hit fairways, I think the rest of the game will be in good shape."

Starting the week 12th in the Race to Dubai standings and too far back to win the Harry Vardon Trophy, Hatton leads the tournament on nine under - one ahead of France's Victor Perez - as he looks to close out a ninth DP World Tour title.

"It was a good day," said Hatton, a two-time runner-up at the DP World Tour Championship. "It was tricky - the greens were so fast on the back nine. Every putt I had coming in I think from the 13th was just unbelievably fast. Really happy with how I putted today.

"I know tomorrow is going to be a tough day. I've got enough experience down these last few holes to know that anything can happen. I'll just go out tomorrow and try my best. I know I can play well around here, and that's what I'll try to do."

title: Bryson DeChambeau reveals new career venture days before deadline on Tour decision
article_text:
Bryson DeChambeau has unveiled a new project that has been years in the making.

On Friday, the two-time U.S Open champion announced The Orchard, a golf and residential community situated in the McFarlane Ranch in Clovis, California.

In collaboration with his long-time real estate partner, Cook Land Company, DeChambeau has detailed his vision for what is dubbed a "one-of-a-kind golf and residential community."

This particular location is home to YouTube star DeChambeau who attended Clovis East High School until his graduation in 2012.

“The Central Valley has always been a community built on hard work, character, and discipline," DeChambeau said in an official press release.

"Having grown up here and attended Clovis East High School, I feel a deep responsibility to give back to the region that provided me with so much.

“This is a profound opportunity for my team and I to work with the Cook family to help revitalize the area by investing in a project that uses golf to truly serve the community.”

The Orchard will feature a championship 18-hole course, along with world-class practice facilities.

But it will also cater to all facets of the local community, with it slated to include an on-site farmers market, as well as amenities designed to expand access to golf for local schools and its children.

Furthermore, particular attention has been paid to the design of each hole on the course, with a different variety of fruit or nut true at each one.

This has been done to enrich the golfing experience and make it more distinctive.

According to DeChambeau, he has been working on this project since 2022 in coordination with the City of Clovis and Fresno County as it pertains to getting all the necessary approvals for development.

“Ultimately, it's time to make a better future for our next generation,” DeChambeau added.

“We are dedicated to ‘Building Stars of the Future,’ and with continued support from the community, it is our hope that we can bring this project to the community faster so that everyone in the world can come and enjoy the fruits of our labor here in the Central Valley.”

The announcement of the 33-year-old's venture into golf course design came just days before the November 16 deadline for him to declare whether he will apply for DP World Tour membership for the 2027 season.

He is eligible to do so based on being a recent major winner, and could yet follow Sergio Garcia who announced his intention to return to the European circuit following the collapse of LIV Golf.

There is a lot of debate surrounding whether these star-studded names - who have been forced to leave with their options now limited - should be welcomed back to the DP World Tour with open arms after LIV's Saudi Arabian funding was pulled.

But for somebody like Rory McIlroy - who refused to join the breakaway league when it began in 2022 - having the likes of his old foe DeChambeau return would benefit the tours going forward.

“I think a name like Bryson DeChambeau and everything he brings with him, good and bad, he brings eyeballs, which is a good thing for tournaments,” McIlroy stated.

“Honestly, I’m certainly not in his shoes, and nor would I ever want to be, but it doesn’t seem like he’s got many options. You know, if he wants to play competitive golf, it doesn’t seem like he’s got many options.”

title: McIlroy fades as Hatton leads in Dubai
article_text:
Rory McIlroy's hopes of winning a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title faded as he fell four shots behind leader Tyrrell Hatton after three rounds of the season-ending DP World Tour Championship.

Northern Irishman McIlroy started Saturday tied for the lead with Hatton but, while the Englishman remained at the top of the field with a four-under-par 68, McIlroy fell away with a 72 at the Earth Course in Dubai.

Hatton, on nine under for the tournament, holds a one-shot lead over France's Victor Perez as he bids for a first DP World Tour Championship, while Sweden's Mikael Lindberg is third on six under.

McIlroy is joint fourth in a group of four players which includes Spain's Eugenio Chacarra, the current leader in the Race to Dubai standings.

Six-time major champion McIlroy began the tournament trailing Chacarra by more than 500 points, but knowing a win would guarantee him an eighth season-long crown to equal the tally set by Scotland's Colin Montgomerie.

McIlroy will clinch the title if he finishes ahead of Chacarra and in the top four.

McIlroy took the outright lead with an eagle three on the par-five seventh, before bogeys on the eighth, ninth and 10th.

A birdie on the 14th was followed by another dropped shot on the 15th, but McIlroy finished with a birdie at the par-five 18th after narrowly missing a six-foot eagle putt.

Hatton scrambled a par at the last after driving into the water and finding a greenside bunker with his approach shot.

He will play alongside Perez, who carded a 67, on the final day.

"It would mean a lot to go on and win tomorrow," said Hatton.

"There is a lot that can change. The course is playing difficult this week and there's a lot of fantastic players just behind. It is going to be a tough day."

Spain's Jon Rahm, who could clinch the Race to Dubai title with victory on Sunday, fell six shots off the lead with a third consecutive 71.

Chacarra, four shots adrift off the lead after two rounds, carded a 68 that included nine birdies, three bogeys and a double bogey.

McIlroy will play alongside Englishman Dan Bradbury, who climbed to four under with a stunning 66.

Chacarra, four shots adrift off the lead after two rounds, carded a 68 that included nine birdies, three bogeys and a double bogey.

Lindberg will play in the penultimate group alongside Australia's 2013 Masters winner Adam Scott, who went round a 67.

title: DP World Tour Championship: Rory McIlroy suffers big Race to Dubai setback as Tyrrell Hatton takes lead into final day
article_text:
Rory McIlroy and Eugenio Chacarra sit in a share of fourth at the DP World Tour Championship, as both players battle for Race to Dubai victory; Tyrrell Hatton holds a one-shot lead; watch the final day live on Sunday from 6.30am on Sky Sports Golf

Tyrrell Hatton takes a one-shot lead into the final day of the DP World Tour Championship, as Rory McIlroy suffered a big setback in his bid to win the Race to Dubai.

McIlroy held a share of the halfway lead at Jumeriah Golf Estates and briefly grabbed the solo advantage at the par-five seventh, only to lose ground with three consecutive bogeys around the turn.

A closing birdie salvaged a level-par 72 and kept him on five under, four strokes behind Hatton in a share of fourth, leaving McIlroy with work to do to claim a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title.

Hatton posted a four-under 68 to edge ahead of Victor Perez, who is currently projected to win one 10 PGA Tour cards up for grabs via the Race to Dubai rankings, while Sweden's Mikael Lindberg sits three strokes back in third.

McIlroy needs at least solo fourth or better to have any chance of leapfrogging Eugenio Chacarra in the standings, with both players locked on five under alongside Adam Scott and Francesco Laporta going into the final day of the season.

McIlroy missed several birdie chances over his opening holes and fell two behind when Hatton - chasing a ninth DP World Tour title - produced a brilliant 10-foot eagle at the par-five second.

Hatton got up and down to save par at the fourth but lost his outright advantage when Perez posted back-to-back birdies from the sixth, moving the Frenchman to seven under.

McIlroy ended his par streak with a brilliant eagle at the par-five seventh, moving him one ahead when Perez finished his front nine with a bogey, only for The Masters champion to lose momentum around the turn.

He failed to get up and down to save par at the eighth and then bogeyed his next two holes, as Hatton fired back-to-back birdies around the turn to temporarily jump into a three-shot advantage.

Perez charged towards the lead with a three-birdie run from the 15th, which saw him move alongside Hatton when the Englishman cancelled out a 15-foot birdie at the 14th by failing to scramble par from the sand at the next.

McIlroy made the same birdie-bogey run to drop to four under and fall back behind Chacarra in the Race to Dubai standings, as the Spaniard birdied four of his last six holes to close a four-under 68.

Hatton's wonderful approach into the par-four 16th set up a close-range birdie, before he recovered from finding water off the final tee to scramble par and remain one ahead of Perez.

McIlroy threatened a second eagle of the day after a brilliant approach into the par-five last, although missed from seven feet and had to settle for a closing birdie.

Tyrrell Hatton, speaking after his third-round 68: "It was a good day. It was tricky - the greens were so fast on the back nine. Every putt I had coming in I think from the 13th was just unbelievably fast. Really happy with how I putted today.

"I know tomorrow is going to be a tough day. I've got enough experience down these last few holes to know that anything can happen. I'll just go out tomorrow and try my best. I know I can play well around here, and that's what I'll try to do."

Eugenio Chacarra, heading into the final day tied-fourth: "I just want to win the tournament - I'm not far away. I know if I win the tournament, I win the ranking, so that's what I wanted to do in Abu Dhabi and I want to do it here.

"I think all of my goals have been done this season, so I'm just playing free. Not a lot of people can enjoy this moment and have a chance to win The Race to Dubai. So I'm going to have a chance tomorrow, and I'm going to go try and enjoy it as much as possible."

title: 106-year-old college football home renamed after historic $70m deal with $8bn giants
article_text:
Another college record has fallen as schools across the US follow their NFL cousins in supercharging their brands.

In the NFL, the Tennessee Titans are poised to become the next team to move into a new, multi-billion dollar arena following the Buffalo Bills, who moved into Highmark Stadium this offseason.

The Cleveland Browns also have a new stadium under construction, while the Washington Commanders, Chicago Bears, Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos are all proposing new homes.

The changing face of the NCAA has allowed college athletes to maximise their value through NIL (Name, Image and Likeness) deals.

In college, the stadium landscape is a little different, with most teams choosing to focus on redeveloping their iconic stadiums and maximising their value.

Schools are also able to cash in on their appeal with kit deals and patch agreements, but the sponsorship of stadia is perhaps the most lucrative route to a fortune.

The Washington Huskies have cashed in following an earlier decision to split the rights to their football and basketball homes.

A 10-year deal with Alaska Airlines that benefited the University of Washington to the tune of $42 million for the naming rights to the football stadium and basketball arena expired in 2025.

That number will more than double after a $70 million, 10-year naming rights deal with Columbia Bank was agreed that will rename Husky Stadium, their home since 1920 as Colombia Bank Stadium.

The $8 billion finance giants have agreed to a $7 million a year deal for the next decade that is subject to Board of Regents approval.

"This is a historic long-term partnership for Washington Athletics and the University of Washington," athletic director Pat Chun said in a press release.

"Columbia Bank Stadium will be the most visible expression of the relationship, but the greater opportunity is what we can build together for our student-athletes, students and communities across Washington.

"At a time of extraordinary change in college athletics, partnerships like this help us create sustainable resources, expand opportunities, and continue investing in the people and programs that make Washington special."

A $280 million redevelopment of the stadium took place in 2013 that increased capacity to more than 70,000 and it remains one of the most atmospheric in college sports.

Per the Sports Business Journal, the deal represents a record football stadium naming rights partnership for college sport.

It also means that the Huskies sporting arenas will bring them in almost $10million a year, following a deal for their basketball home earlier this year.

In March, Alaska Airlines recommitted to a 10-year agreement on the basketball arena, worth $28.4million but the football stadium deal has blown that out of the water.

The Huskies have a 5-4 record this year, and face Michigan State this weekend before their final home game of the season sees reigning national champions Indiana at Colombia Bank Stadium.

title: NCAA and Modelo partner; Columbia Bank puts name to Washington stadium
article_text:
Modelo, the Mexico-based beer brand, has signed up to become a commercial partner of US college sports' NCAA governing body.

Through a tie-up made public yesterday, Constellation Brands-owned Modelo becomes the first official beer partner of that collegiate sporting body. This adds, in terms of a college sports presence, to Modelo's existing deal with the College Football Playoffs, and its specific individual partnerships with 28 NCAA member schools.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The NCAA is now able to bring alcohol brands in as sponsors (and to have alcohol advertised during its championship events), after a long-running ban was lifted at the start of July. The ban has been lifted as part of efforts to generate an extra $300 million in revenue for the NCAA, over the next six years.

The March Madness high-profile college basketball tournament will act as the centerpiece of this partnership, with Modelo set to advertise around that time period across broadcast, digital, and social media channels.

Modelo will have exclusive rights in the beer category to activate across NCAA domestic broadcasts, while it now also holds rights to use official NCAA marks and logos in its retail programming and consumer promotions.

In addition, the brand will activate at select NCAA championship events, as well as in "priority markets."

Finally, Modelo now holds exclusive ready-to-drink (RTD) sponsorship rights. As such, RTD brand SpikedAde – bought up by Constellation Brands last month – will be promoted.

Mallika Monteiro, executive vice president and managing director of beer brands at Constellation Brands, commented: "Few things inspire the pride, dedication and fighting spirit quite like we see in college sports fans, and Modelo has spent years building a presence alongside them at the biggest moments."

Outside of college sports, Modelo also sponsors multiple Major League Soccer franchises, including Inter Miami, Atlanta United, and LAFC.

Earlier this year, it sponsored coverage of soccer's 2026 FIFA World Cup – held across Mexico, the US, and Canada – on US Spanish-language broadcaster Telemundo.

In terms of NCAA activity, meanwhile, late August saw the organization announce a wide-ranging new agreement with the sports media and marketing technology firm Playfly Sports, which has now become an NCAA sponsorship sales agent.

Elsewhere in college sports, the University of Washington, in that US state, has brought in Columbia Bank as the new title sponsor for its college football program home stadium.

That venue – from January 1 – will be called the Columbia Bank Stadium, while the bank has also become the fourth 'signature partner' – the top level of sponsor – for Washington University. It joins Pepsico, Starbucks, and Alaska Airlines, as a signature partner.

Columbia Bank has become an exclusive partner of the Washington Athletics program, in addition.

It also plans to engage with student athletes there around financial education and management.

The university has worked with the One Roof Sports & Entertainment agency to develop the partnership deal.

Robert J. Jones, president at the University of Washington, commented: "This is the kind of partnership great public universities should be building. It brings together two institutions with deep roots in Washington and creates opportunities that extend well beyond athletics."

title: Argentina eventually see-off Italy in scrappy affair in Genoa
article_text:
Italy’s response to last week’s 66-7 Nations Championship humbling by South Africa ultimately came up just short as Gonzalo Quesada’s side fell 19-14 to Argentina in Genoa, but there was enough fight on show to suggest the Azzurri are heading back vaguely in the right direction.

The home side made all the early running and struck inside four minutes when Leonardo Marin produced a delightful grubber kick for Monty Ioane to gather and score in the corner. Tommaso Allan added an excellent touchline conversion and Italy looked comfortably the better side despite Argentina enjoying plenty of possession.

Much of that was down to the outstanding Manuel Zuliani. The flanker was everywhere during the opening exchanges, repeatedly bailing Italy out with breakdown steals deep inside his own 22. One turnover became two, then three, as Zuliani turned into an absolute menace for the Pumas.

Italy’s scrum was also causing serious problems. Danilo Fischetti and Simone Ferrari got on top of Boris Wenger and Francisco Moreno, while Federico Ruzza pinched lineout ball and Niccolò Cannone carried hard through the middle.

Yet for all their territorial dominance, Italy only had seven points to show for it. Marin impressed with ball in hand and an interception, Paolo Odogwu produced some meaty collisions, but chances repeatedly went begging.

Argentina finally made Italy pay just before the break. Guido Petti disrupted the Italian lineout, Pedro Rubiolo and Pablo Matera dragged the visitors into the contest, and a catch-and-drive score levelled matters at 7-7 going into half-time.

The second half belonged largely to the Pumas. Tomás Albornoz began pulling the strings, Mateo Carreras and Rodrigo Isgró found space out wide, and Argentina’s six visits into the Italian 22 yielded enough points to build a 19-7 advantage.

To Italy’s credit, they refused to fold. Sustained pressure eventually brought a penalty try on 65 minutes, with Cannone unlucky not to be awarded the score himself.

A late fightback followed from the home side, but Paolo Garbisi’s botched final-play touchfinder with the game hanging in the balance let Argentina off the hook.

title: Courtney Lawes hospitalised amid battle with 'serious bacterial infection'
article_text:
Sale Sharks lock Courtney Lawes is recovering after being hospitalised with a serious bacterial infection that had entered his bloodstream.

The 37-year-old hasn’t featured for Sale since their Investec Champions Cup loss to Glasgoe on October 17.

The former England and British & Irish Lions forward revealed in a LinkedIn post that he had been treated with antibiotics. Lawes said the uncertainty around his recovery had been the biggest challenge.

“After feeling pretty rough and eventually ending up in hospital, it turned out I had a serious bacterial infection that had made its way into my bloodstream.

“I’ve spent the best part of 20 years playing professional rugby, so I’m no stranger to injuries, pain and the occasional hospital visit. But this was something completely different.

“When you’re injured, there’s normally a fairly clear process. You know what’s wrong, you have a rehabilitation plan and, more often than not, you have a rough idea of when you’ll be back.

“This time, none of those things have been particularly clear.

“It’s a strange feeling going from being fit, healthy and training every day to suddenly finding yourself in a hospital bed, relying on antibiotics and doctors to get you back on your feet.

“And I think that’s probably been the biggest challenge. The uncertainty.

“I’m used to being able to take some control over my recovery. Put the work in, do the rehab, trust the process and eventually see the results.

“Unfortunately, this isn’t quite something you can squat your way out of.”

Lawes said the spell in hospital had also given him a chance to reflect on how easily athletes can take their health for granted.

“It’s also given me a bit of perspective.

“As athletes, we spend so much time worrying about performance, fitness and getting the most out of ourselves that it’s easy to take something as simple as being healthy for granted.”

Lawes said he was feeling much better, although he gave no timetable for a return to action with Sale. He also thanked the doctors, nurses and hospital staff who cared for him.

“I’m feeling much better now, thankfully, although there’s still some uncertainty around what the next few weeks will look like and how my return to play will look.

“For now, I’m just looking forward to getting back to normality. Spending time with the family, getting back into a routine and hopefully getting a sweat on sooner rather than later.

“A massive thank you to all the doctors, nurses and hospital staff who have looked after me. It’s been a real eye opener seeing the work you do firsthand, and I’m incredibly grateful.”

Mirra Andreeva breaks a Serena Williams WTA Finals record and equals Justine Henin feat with latest win
article_text:
Mirra Andreeva’s fine WTA Finals form continued with an emphatic win on Friday, and the Russian broke a record previously held by Serena Williams as a result.

World No 3 Andreeva has not looked phased in her maiden singles appearance at the year-end championships this week, beating Elina Svitolina and Aryna Sabalenka — both with a 6-4, 6-0 scoreline — in her opening two matches of the event.

Victory in those two matches meant that the 19-year-old was already confirmed as the winner of her group heading into the final day of round-robin action, with the Russian unexpectedly facing compatriot and close friend Diana Shnaider, the alternate stepping following Karolina Muchova’s withdrawal due to illness.

Andreeva was broken in her opening service game of the match but was in complete control after that, claiming another emphatic victory in Indian Wells with a 6-2, 6-1 triumph over the world No 11.

On her WTA Finals debut, Andreeva is the only unbeaten player left in the singles draw, and she will take on Jessica Pegula in a highly-anticipated semi-final on Saturday night.

However, regardless of how she fares across the rest of the campaign, she has already made WTA Finals history.

While Andreeva qualified for the 2025 WTA Finals in doubles alongside Shnaider, she just missed out on making her singles debut in Riyadh.

But the Russian has wasted little time on her singles debut at the prestigious tournament, with dominant victories over Svitolina, Sabalenka, and Shnaider in her first-ever matches at the event.

Aged 19 years and 193 days at the start of the event, Andreeva is now the youngest woman in the 21st century to win the first three WTA Finals singles matches of her career.

As per Opta Ace, this breaks the record of Serena Williams, who was 20 years and 34 days old at the 2001 WTA Finals. That event was held as a straight knockout, with the tennis great defeating Silvia Farina Ella, Justine Henin, and Sandrine Testud in her first three matches to reach the final.

The next youngest women to achieve this feat this century are Petra Kvitova (21 years and 230 days) in 2011, Garbine Muguruza (22 years and 17 days) in 2015, and Sloane Stephens (25 years and 216 days) in 2018.

Andreeva will be hoping she can follow in the footsteps of both Williams and Kvitova, who both went on to claim the WTA Finals on their event debuts.

Furthermore, Andreeva has also matched another WTA Finals record set by former world No 1 Henin almost two decades ago.

Having dropped just four games against both Svitolina and Sabalenka and then only three games against Shnaider, Andreeva dropped a total of just 11 games across the round-robin stage.

This is now a joint-record for the least games dropped since the event introduced the round-robin format in 2003, matching Henin from 2007.

Henin beat Jelena Jankovic 6-2, 6-2, Anna Chakvetadze 6-1, 7-6(4), and Marion Bartoli 6-0, 6-0 during her campaign, and would go on to win the title that week.

title: MotoGP awards US media rights to ESPN through 2028
article_text:
MUMBAI: MotoGP is shifting into a higher gear in the Americas, with ESPN taking the championship’s US broadcasting rights for the next two seasons and extending a partnership with the racing series in Latin America that stretches back nearly 25 years.

The two-year media rights agreement will cover the 2027 and 2028 seasons, making ESPN the exclusive media rights holder for MotoGP in the US. The broadcaster will carry the championship across its linear television networks and platforms, giving American audiences access to every race weekend.

From 2027, Grand Prix events in the US will be shown either live or on a same-day delayed basis. That means fans will not have to wait until the following day to catch the action, although the precise broadcast timing will vary by event.

The agreement also strengthens ESPN’s existing position in Latin America. The network will continue to provide extensive MotoGP coverage across key markets in the region, with races available on ESPN networks and through Disney+ Plan Premium. The arrangement extends coverage across 18 countries, where ESPN and MotoGP have worked together since 2002.

The deal also leaves room for local broadcasters to get in on the action. Selected events in Argentina and Brazil can be sublicensed to free-to-air television channels, giving the championship an opportunity to reach viewers beyond subscription television and streaming services.

For MotoGP, the US expansion is an important step in its efforts to grow the sport in a market where it sees an opportunity to build a larger following. ESPN’s established sports audience and distribution network offer the championship a prominent platform to introduce motorcycle racing to viewers who may not yet be regular followers.

MotoGP deputy CEO Carlos Ezpeleta said the agreement marked an important milestone in the championship’s growth strategy across the Americas. He pointed to ESPN’s standing as a leading sports broadcaster and its connection with audiences in both the US and Latin America as key reasons for the partnership.

The expanded arrangement is also a continuation of a relationship that has developed over almost a quarter of a century. ESPN first began carrying MotoGP in Latin America in 2002, building an audience across the region before adding the US to its rights portfolio under the new agreement.

ESPN head of global sports and talent office Freddy Rolón said the partnership had grown from its Latin American roots into a wider opportunity across the broadcaster’s international business. He added that the expanded rights would allow ESPN to connect more audiences with the championship.

The agreement gives MotoGP a two-pronged distribution strategy in the Americas: an exclusive broadcaster in the US and continued television and streaming coverage across Latin America, with free-to-air sublicensing opportunities in selected markets.

With the 2027 season marking the start of the new deal, the championship has two years to build on its existing Latin American following while putting its racing spectacle in front of a wider American audience.

title: Springboks' nightmare 2027 Rugby World Cup route revealed
article_text:
South Africa's 21-19 defeat to France on Friday night has offered a worrying glimpse of what could await them at the 2027 Rugby World Cup.

Rassie Erasmus is chasing a third successive world title in Australia, but the draw has done the Springboks few favours.

The world champions could face New Zealand in the quarter-finals before another meeting with France in the last four.

And after Friday's defeat in Paris, that prospect looks even less appealing.

South Africa have been drawn alongside Italy, Georgia and Romania in Pool B.

Erasmus will expect his side to finish top, although Italy could provide a decent test.

The expanded 24-team tournament also brings a new round of 16, meaning the Springboks must win four knockout matches to lift the Webb Ellis Cup.

That extra fixture should be manageable if they win their group.

What follows is another matter entirely.

Assuming the leading seeds progress as expected, South Africa would face their greatest rivals, New Zealand, in the quarter-finals.

Victory there could set up a semi-final against France, with England, Ireland or Argentina among the possible opponents in the final.

These are projected opponents, not confirmed fixtures. The route assumes the leading seeds win their pools and progress.

Friday's Nations Championship clash in Paris showed just how difficult another meeting with Les Bleus could be.

France raced into a 21-7 half-time lead, with Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang, Théo Attissogbe and Louis Bielle-Biarrey all crossing.

The Springboks fought back through Cobus Reinach and Malcolm Marx, despite losing Jasper Wiese to a 20-minute red card.

But Manie Libbok missed a conversion that would have levelled the scores, and France held on for a famous victory.

It was their first home win over South Africa since 2005.

The result also came just over three years after the Springboks knocked France out of their home World Cup, winning a remarkable quarter-final 29-28.

Another meeting in Australia would carry plenty of history.

Of course, South Africa have already shown they can survive a brutal knockout draw.

Their 2023 triumph included three victories by a single point.

They edged France 29-28 in the quarter-finals, beat England 16-15 in the semi-finals and then defeated New Zealand 12-11 in the final.

Three matches. Three points between them.

The Springboks also became the first nation to win four men's Rugby World Cups.

Now they have the chance to make it three titles in a row, something no country has previously achieved.

But with New Zealand and France potentially standing between them and the final, Erasmus might need another extraordinary knockout run.

And Friday night's defeat suggests there will be little margin for error.

The tournament takes place in Australia from 1 October to 13 November 2027, with 24 nations divided into six pools of four.

The top two teams from each pool, plus the four best third-placed sides, will advance to the round of 16.

From there, it is straight knockout rugby through to the final in Sydney on 13 November.

title: She is the only British player to reach the final of the WTA Finals in history with Emma Raducanu yet to qualify
article_text:
Emma Raducanu has not played at the year-end WTA Finals so far in her career.

Raducanu is the most recent British Grand Slam champion, having shocked the world in 2021 after winning the US Open as a qualifier.

This enabled the then teenage Raducanu to be boosted up the rankings and to end the year 14th in the race, but this was not enough for her to qualify for the WTA Finals, with the Grand Slam rule not in place at this point.

Although Raducanu has never played at the WTA Finals, one British player was just a set away from the title at the prestigious tournament.

Raducanu was the first British women's singles Grand Slam champion in 44 years when she won the US Open in 2021, with Virginia Wade the one before that.

Before Wade was Sue Barker, who became a Grand Slam champion when she won Roland Garros in 1976. This was not the only big result of Barker's career, as she also reached the final of the WTA Finals in 1977.

Barker did this by beating Martina Navratilova en route to the final, before facing three-time former WTA Finals champion Chris Evert.

The Briton had lost her 10 previous matches against Evert, but Barker made a positive start to this final after winning the first set.

However, Evert showed why she had dominated their head-to-head, as she fought back to beat Barker 2-6, 6-1, 6-1 and claim her fourth and final WTA Finals title.

How many British singles players have qualified for the WTA Finals?

Barker may not have won the WTA Finals title in 1977, but she is still the only British player to have reached the final of the year-end tournament. This was one of three singles appearances Barker made at the WTA Finals, and she also reached the doubles final alongside American Ann Kiyomura in 1979.

Including Barker, only three British players in history have qualified for the WTA Finals in singles, with the aforementioned Wade making eight appearances at the tournament. Wade had success in doubles as well, having won the title alongside Margaret Court in 1975, and she also twice finished as runner-up alongside Frenchwoman Francoise Durr.

The only other British player who has qualified for the WTA Finals in singles is Jo Durie, who did so in 1984, the same year that she also reached the doubles final alongside the aforementioned Kiyomura.

Durie is the last British woman to qualify for the WTA Finals in singles, with Johanna Konta coming the closest to ending this streak in 2016, when she was the first alternate.

title: The DP World Tour Championship title, the Race to Dubai Crown, PGA Tour Dual Membership and Open exemptions: Here's what's at stake on the final day
article_text:
While Tyrrell Hatton targets a first title around the Earth Course, Eugenio Chacarra will hope to hold off Rory McIlroy's attempt to win a record-tying eighth Race to Dubai as he looks to secure the season-long crown.

Other players will be battling it out for both Dual Membership on the PGA Tour and an exemption into next year's Open at St Andrews.

Here is what is at stake for the field on the final day of the DP World Tour Championship.

Tyrrell Hatton has a great record around the Earth Course, but despite a couple of runner-up finishes he has yet to make it over the line with a victory at the DP World Tour Championship.

A prolific Rolex Series winner, the Englishman finished second last week and says he will go out there and try his best as he hopes to hold off not only nearest challenger Victor Perez, but a host of players chasing him that include Race to Dubai number one and two, Eugenio Chacarra and Rory McIlroy.

"I know tomorrow's going to be a tough day," Hatton said. "I've got enough experience down these last few holes to know that anything can happen. I'll just go out tomorrow and try my best."

Eugenio Chacarra fought back during an impressive third round 68 which saw him birdie four of his final six holes to regain his projected spot at the top of the Race to Dubai Rankings delivered by DP World.

Rory McIlroy struggled to build on momentum after an eagle at the seventh and went from holding a two-shot lead to four shots behind playing partner Hatton just three holes later. A level-par 72 means he will go into the final round of the season with it all to do as he sits alongside Chacarra tied fourth on five under par for the tournament.

McIlroy's best chance to win a record-tying eighth Race to Dubai crown is winning outright or finishing solo second (providing Chacarra does not win), but the permutations are more favourable for the three-time winner this season. With Chacarra playing here for just the second time and McIlroy a three-time winner, it's sure to be an exciting final day around the Earth Course.

As part of the Strategic Alliance between the DP World Tour and PGA Tour, the top ten players on the final 2026 Race to Dubai Rankings, not otherwise exempt, will earn Dual Membership on the PGA Tour for 2027.

Race to Dubai leader Chacarra tops that list, followed by fellow multiple-time winners this season Patrick Reed, Casey Jarvis and Jayden Schaper.

While the picture around the final few spots changed hands numerous times on Saturday, it was Mikael Lindberg who made the most significant move, playing his way into ninth position in the race for the ten PGA Tour Dual Membership cards. The Swede made three birdies in a row to finish his round and carded a 69, which puts him on six under for the week in solo third. With that birdie at the last, the 2026 Turkish Airlines Open winner knocked Oliver Lindell down one spot as he leapfrogged Joe Dean to ninth position, while Dean sits in tenth.

Lindell is one of several players who spent time both in and out of that list on Saturday, as well as Francesco Laporta, Dan Bradbury and Nacho Elvira. With the points difference incredibly narrow, we expect a lot of movement tomorrow too. Here's how it looks right now.

For many, there is more on the line that just a card or the title itself, as the first 25 players in the Final Race to Dubai standings for 2026 will earn an exemption into the 155th Open at St Andrews in 2027.

Here's how it looks on the projected rankings of the Race to Dubai after the third round, showing who already has an exemption and who could be in line for one depending on the outcome of tomorrow's DP World Tour Championship finale.

title: Ma'asi-White marks landmark with try as Sharks beat Chiefs in cup
article_text:
Centre Rekeiti Ma'asi-White scored a try on his 50th appearance for Sale as the Sharks turned up the power to beat Exeter Chiefs and continue their impressive form in the Prem Rugby Cup.

While the league campaign has been a struggle, Alex Sanderson's team have shown up well in Pool A and a bonus-point win at Corpacq Stadium stretched their lead at the top.

Exeter, whose discipline let them down, struck first in the 11th minute with a try by left-wing Charlie Poynton, but Sale's response was instant as wing Alex Wills outjumped the Chiefs defence to grab a cross-kick and touch down.

The sin-binning of Paul Brown-Bampoe for taking Wills out in the air gave the home side a man advantage for 10 minutes and they exploited it with a try by Ma'asi-White.

Ben Coen had an opportunity to cut the deficit with a penalty, only to strike the post from 40 metres out, but the Exeter stand-off made amends with the last play of the half, stepping over from Zack Wimbush's pass to score the Chiefs' second try.

Exeter, with 145kg prop Ehren Painter back and making his presence felt after almost two years out with a knee injury, were dominating the scrum but it was the Sharks' driving maul which came to the fore after the break to pull them clear.

Three maul tries, one from hooker Alfie Longstaff and two for his replacement Nathan Jibulu did the damage with Sale adding a penalty try as Exeter illegally disrupted another drive close to their line. Hooker Max Norey was yellow-carded.

Exeter did though manage a try-scoring bonus point with prop Archie McArthur and captain Sam Wolstenholme crossing in the second half to nudge them off the bottom of Pool A.

"Every game's important because we've got to try and find some winning momentum.

"I've just said to the lads, 'I'm not going to try to find positives for you every week'. If you start finding positives in losing when you shouldn't, what you do is you actually start to accept being a loser, and I'm not going to let the lads just accept that tonight was OK.

"They've got to learn quicker. What annoys me is everybody says, 'these lads have got to play'. Sometimes there's a reason why they don't play and it's because they do silly things. We see them doing them in training and it makes you doubt picking them, because you're worried about what might happen in the game. The problem is that's what's been reflected tonight.

"I'm not going to keep saying, 'well done, we scored some good tries', because so much of the territory we gave up was completely brainless territory.

"The penalty count is against us anyway, but if we hadn't been able to get scrum pens, the penalty count would have been ridiculous against us."

title: Indian Football League extends title sponsorship pact with Star Cement
article_text:
The Indian Football League (IFL) has renewed its partnership with Star Cement, which will continue as the league’s title sponsor for the entire 2026–27 season.

The tournament will henceforth be referred to as the Star Cement Indian Football League 2026-27.

Star Cement, the leading cement brand in Northeast India and a rapidly expanding name nationwide, has built a reputation in the infrastructure industry for its dependability, durability, and toughness. The firm has consistently associated its brand image with sports, supporting athletes and athletic programs as part of a broader goal of fostering excellence, perseverance, and community involvement.

The renewal prolongs a collaboration that commenced on March 11, 2026, when the AIFF and Star Cement entered into an agreement for the 2025-26 season. That campaign marked the league’s inaugural season following its rebranding from the I-League, with Star Cement being the first title sponsor of the competition in its new format.

Mr. Nildeep Mondal, Chief Executive Officer, Indian Football League, said, “Star Cement’s decision to continue as our title sponsor is a strong vote of confidence in the Indian Football League. They backed the league in its first season under a new identity, and we are delighted to carry that partnership into a full home-and-away campaign. With new clubs, new venues and wider broadcast reach this season, the league is growing in every direction, and it means a great deal to have a partner who shares our ambition for Indian football. We thank Star Cement for their continued support and look forward to building on what we started together last season.”

Mr. Pradeep Purohit, Chief Operating Officer, Star Cement, said, “Our continued partnership with the Indian Football League reflects our belief in the potential of Indian football and the importance of sustained support for its growth. With our roots in the Northeast, we share a special connection with the passion the game inspires. The IFL brings that passion to a national stage, giving clubs and players across the country a platform to earn recognition and inspire young talent. We are proud to continue as title sponsor and look forward to supporting the league as it reaches more communities and builds a stronger future for Indian football.”

The initial season of the collaboration proved fruitful for the league, as viewership for the IFL was quadruple that of the 2024-25 season. With the updated agreement, Star Cement will once more be involved in the league’s branding and promotional efforts during the season.

The Star Cement Indian Football League 2026-27 began on October 30, as Real Kashmir FC faced off against newcomers Nagaland United SC at the TRC Stadium in Srinagar. Eleven teams are engaged in a complete home-and-away round-robin format, with each team participating in 20 matches before the season ends on March 20, 2027.

Member, League Managing Committee and Owner of Shillong Lajong FC, Mr. Larsing Ming Sawyan, said, “Star Cement came on board when the Indian Football League was taking its first steps under a new identity, and their decision to continue as title sponsor shows real faith in where the league is heading. Last season gave us a glimpse of what is possible, and with a full home-and-away campaign, new clubs and new venues this time, we are confident the league will keep growing from strength to strength. On behalf of the entire league, I would like to thank Star Cement for standing by Indian football and continuing this journey with us.”

All matches are broadcast live on DD Sports, and some games are also aired on Unite8 Sports. Every match is broadcasted live on Z5, WAVES, and the Unite8 Sports official YouTube channel.

title: Dinner For Five (Billion): A look at the NFL’s media rights “menu”
article_text:
Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk reported recently that the NFL has presented prospective bidders on its new five-game media rights package a “menu” of options from which to choose. If the league is to hit its typical mid-May timeline for the release of this year’s schedule, those orders probably need to be placed in the next few weeks. Sports Media Watch examines this broadcasting “menu,” with a look at who could be at the table and what their appetite might look like.

The league has announced a record nine-game international slate for the 2026 season. Six of these are set for European markets: three in London, plus one each in Madrid, Munich and Paris. These typically air in a 9:30 AM ET window, but could also be part of the 1:00 regional games.

Two additional games are set for Rio de Janeiro (featuring the Dallas Cowboys) and Mexico City (hosted by the San Francisco 49ers). Both of these games could air in primetime or in the afternoon. There will not be a game — in Rio or elsewhere — on the Friday of Week 1; that was only allowed the last two years thanks to a calendar quirk.

The one international game that does have a date is the 49ers-Rams game in Melbourne on September 10. The game will kickoff in primetime on Thursday night, which corresponds to late Friday morning in Australia. That opening Thursday is typically occupied by the NFL’s season opener, which has been pushed back to Wednesday night this year.

Since the addition of out-of-home viewing to Nielsen audience measurement in 2020, the NFL has cracked the code on getting big audiences: occasions when Americans are likely to be gathered in homes together with family and friends. Out-of-home viewing gives a boost to viewership on Sundays, but is particularly strong on holidays like Thanksgiving and Christmas, and the days surrounding them. It’s why the Thanksgiving afternoon games are consistently the most-watched games of any season.

With this in mind, the NFL seeks to take advantage of any available moment over the critical holiday stretch. Reports indicate the league is considering selling a new “Thanksgiving Eve” game on Wednesday night — a night that has typically produced strong results for the NBA. That will be followed by the traditional Thanksgiving Day tripleheader, with home games for Detroit and Dallas, and then a Black Friday slate that could expand to multiple games.

Christmas Eve falls on a Thursday night, so could feature a game as part of Amazon’s Thursday Night Football or another partner. Christmas Day will feature a tripleheader, after the commissioner went on the record last year to confirm there will always be three games on Christmas Day, regardless of the day of the week the holiday falls.

The NFL is forbidden by law from televising Saturday games through the first Saturday of September to the second Saturday of December as part of the 1961 Sports Broadcasting Act’s conditions to grant the league an antitrust exemption. That would leave just four regular-season Saturdays (December 19 and 26 and January 2 and 9) for the NFL, and the league will take full advantage of them. The Week 15 games clash with the first round of the College Football Playoff on ESPN and TNT, but the league has not been shy from scheduling marquee games on broadcast TV opposite the CFP.

The next two Saturdays are wide open, and there’s no reason we couldn’t see a tripleheader on both dates. Week 18 contractually belongs to ESPN/ABC, which will air a season-finale doubleheader to be set after the results of Week 17.

All of these special entrees are a part of the league’s aggressive media strategy. The NFL is seeking to force its current partners — for whom NFL inventory is an existential asset — to pay higher rights fees, while also stripping them of inventory to sell in smaller packages. All of the league’s primary partners (ESPN, NBC, FOX, CBS, Amazon) are theoretically able to consider these smaller packages, but the point is really to sell them to outside parties for a little extra cash.

YouTube was recently reported as the frontrunner to acquire a five-game package that could include any of the options above. YouTube streamed the Rio game last year on a one-year deal, and parent company Google is the exclusive distributor of the Sunday Ticket package. Netflix and FOX were also mentioned as competing for the five-game package.

Some mouths additionally need to be fed thanks to prior contractual agreements. Peacock is owed a streaming-exclusive game, which was scheduled for a December Saturday in 2023 and 2025 and featured the Rio game in 2024. NFL Network has to carry a seven-game slate, which in the past has featured a mix of Sunday-morning international games and December Saturdays. Netflix will return with another Christmas Day doubleheader, with FOX — the only partner contractually linked to Christmas when the current rights deals were announced — airing a third game.

Beyond that, is there any limit to the number of carve-outs the league could make? And is there any limit to the number of partners? Perhaps Apple TV could get a game or two for the right price. What about TikTok, in pursuit of the league’s desire to get in front of young people? There’s evidently no reason to rule out anyone willing to put up the cash for a slice of NFL inventory.

title: Canal+ acquires multi-territory broadcast rights to Icons Cup South Africa
article_text:
Canal+ has acquired the broadcast rights to the first Icons Cup South Africa through a multi-territory agreement with the Icons Series. The partnership puts the cross-sport golf event on SuperSport via DStv. It covers Sub-Saharan Africa, France and select international territories, so the new event has a pay-TV home in its host region and in Canal+’s domestic market. Terms were not disclosed.

SuperSport will show the morning sessions on SuperSport Grandstand and the afternoon sessions on SuperSport Golf. Additional coverage and highlights will run on SuperSport Blitz and DStv CatchUp. The three-day event takes place at The Links at Fancourt in George from 11 to 13 December 2026. Team South Africa, captained by Ernie Els, plays José María Olazábal’s Team World, and the squads include players from rugby, cricket, football, golf, swimming and tennis.

Icons Series chief content officer Chris Sice said the agreement marked a major milestone for the series. “By pairing premium golf coverage with entertainment-led storytelling, mic’d-up access, and high-tempo matchplay, we’re delivering a fast-paced, lean-forward live show,” Sice said.

Rendani Ramovha, Canal+ senior vice president for sports content in English- and Portuguese-speaking Africa, said the company was pleased to bring the tournament to Sub-Saharan African audiences.

The rights deal gives the Icons Cup the second half of its commercial base. Earlier this month, Heineken Beverages signed a two-year partnership that relies partly on broadcast integrations for its Windhoek, Savanna and Amarula activations. With SuperSport now confirmed, those integrations have a channel and a pay-TV audience across the region.

SuperSport already carries LIV Golf, which held its first South African event in Johannesburg in March. The Icons Cup is a different product. It is sold on Springbok and Proteas names rather than tour professionals, so it can reach viewers who would watch AB de Villiers putt before they would watch a regular tour event. The three-day format and in-house production also make it straightforward to programme across two channels in December.

Since completing its takeover of MultiChoice in 2025, Canal+ can buy content once and use it in both its African and French markets. Here it gets an event staged in South Africa that also has international names for its home audience.

The Icons Series has now signed both a headline sponsor and a broadcaster before its African debut has been played. Heineken’s deal runs for two years, but the length of the broadcast agreement was not disclosed.

title: Kumamoto Masters: Watanabe Wins Thriller
article_text:
Koki Watanabe reached his second final of the year with a come-from-behind effort against Kunlavut Vitidsarn at the Kumamoto Masters Japan 2026.

Incidentally, Watanabe’s only other final this year was also on home soil – at the DAIHATSU Japan Open in July. The home hope trailed in the second half of the decider, with Vitidsarn taking a three-point lead at 18-15, but Watanabe was tenacious and saved one match point before converting his own second opportunity, 14-21 21-11 23-21.

In the final, Watanabe takes on Lakshya Sen, who made his second straight final. Sen, who won the HYLO Open a fortnight ago, got his first win over Alwi Farhan in three matches, 21-12 15-21 21-11.

“It feels very good to play here, last time I was in the semifinals, so it’s a better result this time. Tomorrow I will play with a free mindset, and I won’t be thinking of the result,” said Sen.

In women’s singles, Akane Yamaguchi made her 11th final of the season after semifinal opponent Chen Yu Fei retired due to a foot injury. Yamaguchi has won three out of 10 finals, but will fancy her chances of a fourth title as her nemesis An Se Young isn’t competing in Japan.

Instead, she will take on Wang Zhi Yi, who beat Tomoka Miyazaki 21-10 21-15. Yamaguchi has won their last four encounters.

Men’s doubles saw Aaron Tai/Yap Roy King do their compatriots Aaron Chia/Soh Wooi Yik a favour as they beat Denmark’s Daniel Lundgaard/Mads Vestergaard. Chia/Soh and Lundgaard/Vestergaard are in a tight race to the World Tour Finals, with the Danes slightly ahead at the moment.

title: Springboks could face fine after France defeat
article_text:
The Springboks could face questions over a possible fine following their 21-19 defeat to France, with Rassie Erasmus' latest selection gamble attracting fresh scrutiny.

But another issue has emerged from the Stade de France, this time involving Erasmus himself.

The Springboks coach made three surprise changes to his starting XV just an hour before kick-off, replacing his entire front row.

Ox Nché, Malcolm Marx and Wilco Louw were moved to the bench, with Gerhard Steenekamp, Jan-Hendrik Wessels and Thomas du Toit promoted to the starting side.

Erasmus has shuffled his front row more often than a Las Vegas blackjack dealer. This time, however, his latest gamble has raised questions about a possible punishment.

Under World Rugby Regulation 15.1.2, teams must announce and exchange their starting line-ups and replacements before an international match.

However, the issue is not quite that simple.

All six front-row players were already named in South Africa's matchday squad. Erasmus simply switched three starters with three replacements.

The question is whether those changes were permitted under the Nations Championship's specific match protocols without an injury or another accepted reason.

According to The South African, there have been calls for World Rugby to examine the decision.

Late tactical changes can attract financial penalties in certain competitions, although those sanctions do not automatically apply to Friday's match.

Crucially, no breach has been established, and there is no confirmed fine or disciplinary investigation.

The double World Cup-winning coach insisted the decision was part of his preparations for the 2027 Rugby World Cup.

Speaking after the defeat, Erasmus explained that the coaching staff had been considering the reshuffle for several days.

"We announced our team on Monday, but then we thought maybe we had to change something," he said.

"We waited until the captain's run on Thursday to decide and even then, we were not sure if we should, but we decided shortly before the game, and it was mainly with testing that combination with the Rugby World Cup next year in mind."

title: History-maker Katerina Siniakova secures record sixth WTA year-end World No. 1 doubles ranking presented by PIF
article_text:
History-maker Katerina Siniakova secures record sixth WTA year-end World No. 1 doubles ranking presented by PIF

- Czech star finishes as the WTA World No.1 doubles player following an outstanding season capturing a Tour-leading seven titles

- Siniakova claims a sixth Year-End No. 1 doubles finish, more than any other player

The WTA (Women's Tennis Association) announced Friday that Katerina Siniakova has secured the 2026 WTA Year-End World No. 1 Doubles Ranking presented by PIF, making history with her record sixth year-end finish in the elite ranking position.

Siniakova has enjoyed a remarkable 2026 season capturing a Tour-leading seven doubles titles, with five coming alongside Taylor Townsend and two with Zhang Shuai. Her haul this year saw her win four WTA 1000 tournaments, including the Sunshine Double at the BNP Paribas Open (Indian Wells) and the Miami Open presented by Itaú, in addition to two Grand Slams at Roland-Garros and the US Open and finally the WTA 500 Brisbane International.

Demonstrating outstanding consistency throughout the year, Siniakova reached nine finals in 15 tournaments played, having also finished as runner-up at back-to-back WTA 1000 events at the China Open (Beijing) and the Dongfeng · Voyah Wuhan Open.

She compiled an impressive 54-8 win-loss record across the season and will be looking to finish on a high at the FAGE WTA Finals with her partner Taylor Townsend as they compete at their third consecutive Finals together.

Siniakova has also continued to strengthen her place in WTA history, having held the World No. 1 doubles ranking for 209 weeks as of November 16, 2026. This places her second on the all-time list for most weeks at No. 1 in doubles, behind only WTA legend Martina Navratilova, who held the top spot for 237 weeks.

Valerie Camillo, WTA Chair, said: “Congratulations to Katerina on securing a historic sixth WTA Year-End World No. 1 doubles ranking. Katerina continues to set the standard in women's doubles, making history this season as the first player in the Open Era to achieve the career Grand Slam with two different partners. We are truly privileged to witness such an extraordinary doubles player performing at the very peak of her game.”

Siniakova was presented with the WTA Year-End World No. 1 doubles trophy in recognition of her achievement in the WTA PIF Rankings earlier today at the 2026 FAGE WTA Finals in Indian Wells, California, where the world's leading players come together to celebrate the conclusion of another exciting season on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz.

title: Japan's unlikely leader who turned down the All Blacks
article_text:
Warner Dearns didn't want to go to Japan. Now, he doesn't want to leave.

A decade ago, Dearns' father Grant got a job as a strength and conditioning coach with top-flight Japanese side NEC Green Rockets, taking the family from New Zealand's North Island to a satellite city outside Tokyo.

For Dearns, like most 14-year-olds, swapping class-mates, countries, continents and cultures didn't appeal.

"I said I didn't want to go," says the second row, who will co-captain Japan against England at Allianz Stadium on Saturday.

"My sister and I wanted to stay with our grandma and grandad [in New Zealand]."

But, reluctantly, they made the trip, with Dearns' mother Tanya, a former New Zealand netballer, giving up her own coaching job to help the family settle in Japan.

"The first year or two took a bit to adapt to, it is a very different culture from New Zealand, and the language barrier didn't help much either," remembers Dearns.

"At high school there was no-one else who spoke English. I was the kid who stood out, the only one with blond curly hair, so it was lots of fun."

There were other reasons that Dearns stood out.

Even as a teenager, he stood 6ft 8in tall and weighed more than 19 stone (120.6kg).

In New Zealand, Deans had been more interested in basketball than rugby. But at Kashiwa Senior High School – one of Japan's strongest rugby-playing schools – they moulded him into a monster prospect.

To supplement his size and galloping, long-legged sprint, Dearns' school coaches introduced gymnastics into his training schedule, having him hurdle team-mates and perform flips, to improve his agility around the pitch.

Away from school, he would hit the gym at his dad's employers, working out alongside the likes of former England full-back Alex Goode.

Given that super-charged rugby education, Dearns progressed fast.

Having qualified on residency grounds, he made his Japan debut In November 2021 at just 19.

By France 2023, he was a regular, featuring in all four of the team's matches at the Rugby World Cup.

This past season, he has been a revelation.

He has spent the year back in New Zealand at the Hurricanes on a season's sabbatical, where his bottomless energy, soft hands and line-out prowess helped the Wellington side to their first Super Rugby title in a decade.

Playing alongside All Blacks Jordie Barrett, Ruben Love, Cam Roigard and Peter Lakai, broadened Dearns' horizons once more.

"It was awesome, I got to sit back and see how the boys prepare," Dearns added.

"The All Blacks guys especially lead the way and are part of the leadership group, I got to enjoy playing footy and watch how they do things."

The possibility of Dearns having a more permanent view was raised.

Various figures in New Zealand rugby's scene wondered whether Dearns would be amenable to returning to his homeland, waiting out a three-year Test stand-down requirement and then transferring his allegiance to the All Blacks.

"It was nothing official, it was all sort of hearsay," he says of the possibility of switching sides.

"I had a couple of people coming up to me asking me if I would ever think about it. It was never an option for me."

Dearns is indebted to Japan for the country's role in his development. But Japan is also now home.

Dearns, who now speaks the language fluently and whose son was born in the country, was moved to tears during his adopted nation's anthem at the last World Cup.

His passion shows in the way he plays too.

On his last visit to Twickenham, back in 2022, Dearns set up a try with a break and offload to scrum-half Naoto Saito. In the teams' most recent meeting, in Tokyo in 2024, he assisted another two, one via a brilliant one-handed grab-and-go in midfield.

On both occasions however, Japan ended up on the wrong end of heavy scorelines.

If they are to shock Twickenham, Dearns will need to marshall an extraordinary forward effort, as well as produce showreel moments.

"It is always a set-piece battle and England do a very good job of scrum and line-out, they are obviously very physical," he says.

Dearns has come a long way. But victory on Saturday would be his biggest step yet.

title: Marx one of three Boks benched in last minute change by Erasmus before France
article_text:
South Africa have made a late change for Friday’s Nations Championship clash with France, swapping their entire front row ahead of kick-off.

Jan-Hendrik Wessels, Gerhard Steenekamp and Thomas du Toit will now start at the Stade de France, with World Rugby Player of the Year Malcolm Marx, Ox Nche and Wilco Louw moving to the bench.

The switch completely reverses the front-row combination Rassie Erasmus originally selected for Paris. Louw had been promoted into the starting XV in the only change from the side that beat Italy 66-7, with Du Toit dropping to the replacements.

No reason for the reshuffle was given in the Springboks’ social media announcement, which confirmed the starting trio and corresponding changes to the bench.

“Late change to the Springboks team: The front row of Jan-Hendrik Wessels, Gerhard Steenekamp, and Thomas du Toit will now start, with Malcolm Marx, Ox Nche, and Wilco Louw coming off the bench,” was the message shared on social media.

It is not the first time this year Erasmus has made such an alteration so close to kick-off.

Ahead of South Africa’s meeting with New Zealand in Cape Town in August, the Bok coach also changed all three starting front-rowers late, moving the originally selected trio to the bench and promoting their replacements.

On that occasion, Erasmus explained the decision had been influenced by a change in the weather forecast, with conditions turning out drier than expected.

There is no indication yet that the same reasoning applies in Paris.

The latest move means Du Toit returns to the starting tighthead jersey despite Louw having originally been preferred after Italy managed to deny South Africa their usual scrum dominance in Turin.

Wessels and Steenekamp, meanwhile, are promoted alongside him, leaving Marx, Nche and Louw available to provide a second-half impact.

The remainder of South Africa’s starting XV is unchanged for a match that could prove decisive in the Nations Championship standings.
